subject: Fwd: EdgeGuard SLO request - custom uptime & latency carveout
messages:

To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLO ask for upcoming expansion

Hi Evelyn,

We are ramping a major feature for EdgeGuard this winter and procurement is pushing hard for contract-level commitments. Can Redwood provide a custom uptime and latency SLO for our account? Specifically they want: 
- 99.99% monthly uptime SLA (all regions)
- p95 response latency <= 120ms for text-generation path during business hours (US/EU)

We understand this is stricter than standard, but this customer will guarantee significant committed spend (see deal id below). Please let us know feasibility and any contract/price implications.

Thanks,
Rajiv

EdgeGuard Systems

Evelyn — thanks for the flag. Initial thoughts / items we need to define before an approval discussion: 

1) Exact SLO formula: is uptime computed per month per-region, or weighted global? Need to avoid ambiguity (UTC vs business-hours)
2) Definition of covered endpoints: are they only using the hosted Redwood API endpoints, or will Dedicated/Private variants be involved?
3) Runbook & fallbacks: what fallbacks do we guarantee (e.g., _graceful degrade_ to lower model tier, queued requests, or cross-region failover)?
4) Penalty structure: credits vs termination rights (legal/finance to own this)

From product perspective, we can evaluate a carveout but would require: a) explicit maintenance windows, b) telemetry hooks exposed in Console (per-route latency percentiles), and c) an ops playbook for on-call escalation. We should draft a conditional SLA amendment that lists measurable metrics and allowed exceptions (DDoS, force majeure, customer misconfiguration).

I'll sketch a proposed amendment if we get the traffic/region details and expected ramp schedule.

- Laura
VP Product, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLO ask for upcoming expansion

Heads up on the engineering constraints:

- 99.99% monthly uptime is possible with Dedicated capacity + cross-region failover, but it requires reserved capacity footprint in both US and EU and an ops-runbook to warm standby nodes. If they want hosted without reserved capacity, the risk profile increases and we'd recommend p99 targets rather than p95/p99 latency guarantees.
- p95 <= 120ms depends heavily on model size and prompt complexity. If they're using smaller generation models and we enforce max tokens and caching for common prefixes, achievable. For larger models (>=13B) we should plan for higher latency.
- Telemetry: we'll need to enable per-route latency metrics (not currently exposed to customers at p95 granularity for hosted). That requires a Console change (2-3 sprints) or we can provide a temporary report via SRE exports.

Suggested compromise for contract: Dedicated reservation (or dedicated pool) + latency SLO scoped to the "standard generate" route with token limits and "business-hours" (0900-1900 local). Also include clear maintenance windows and an ops playbook.

I can produce an ops_playbook_edgeguard.txt (stub) and a quick cost estimate for the reserved capacity.

- Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime Engineering

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@edgeguard.com>, Maya Patel <maya.p@edgeguard.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO ask for upcoming expansion (approved with conditions)

Rajiv / Maya — thanks for the patience while we scoped this. After cross-functional review, Redwood can agree to a conditional SLO carveout for EdgeGuard with the following commitments: 

1) Uptime: 99.99% monthly uptime scoped to the hosted API endpoints used by EdgeGuard in US and EU regions, with defined maintenance windows (we will give 48 hours notice for planned maintenance).
2) Latency: p95 response latency <= 120ms for the "standard generate" route during business hours (0900-1900 local) subject to: dedicated reserved capacity in both regions OR an explicit dedicated pool configuration. This must be committed for a minimum 12-month reserved term.
3) Exclusions: force majeure, customer misconfiguration, DDoS beyond our protection threshold, third-party cloud outages, and customer-triggered bulk ingestion.
4) Observability: Redwood will provide per-route latency and request-level traces to EdgeGuard's security contact via SRE exports initially; Console-level per-route dashboards are planned (estimated 2-3 sprints).
5) Credits: service credits capped at 25% of the monthly committed fee for eligible downtime. Full legal language to be in SLA amendment.

Next steps from our side: Marissa will circulate a redline of the amendment (attached). Karthik will provide the reserved capacity estimate and an ops playbook. Laura will draft the SLO metric definitions for the amendment.

Please see the attached amendment (draft_sla_amendment_edgeguard_v1.pdf) and ops playbook. If the terms look acceptable, we can move to DocuSign and the reserved capacity order.

Thanks — cc'ing our product and eng leads to keep everyone aligned.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft_sla_amendment_edgeguard_v1.pdf, ops_playbook_edgeguard.txt
